# GPU placement and transfer

Ideas for placing final input work and transferring data between CPU and GPU. Host-to-device (**H2D**) copies feed GPU consumers; device-to-host (**D2H**) copies return results or metadata to CPU consumers. **Pinned** host storage is page-locked memory usable by the device transfer path; creating it from pageable storage can itself require a host copy. A CUDA **stream** orders device operations, but operations on different streams need explicit dependencies.

Distinguish readiness from ownership: knowing a copy has completed does not mean its destination can be recycled while a later GPU consumer still reads it. Device placement, copy completion and storage lifetime must remain correct; moving work to the GPU is not automatically faster.

Choose the topic whose symptoms match the measured bottleneck. Open only that reference for technique entries and their correctness, lifetime and performance guards.

[Catalog index](../technique_catalog.md)

## GPU input placement

- [GPU input placement](gpu_placement_transfer/gpu_input_placement.md): repeated CPU assembly or uploads, early media widening and cross-socket input allocation.

## Pinned transfer ownership

- [Pinned transfer ownership](gpu_placement_transfer/pinned_transfer_ownership.md): background-copy corruption or memory growth, wrong-device contexts and pageable storage despite configured pinning.

## Transfer calls and readbacks

- [Transfer calls and readbacks](gpu_placement_transfer/transfer_calls_and_readbacks.md): redundant uploads, excessive small-copy submissions and output or metadata readbacks that stall GPU feeding.
